primaryText: Rovnaj kaftə prˈistupnˈik-nˈə-nˈ kona-tˈnˈə-nˈ meždu pročim kunda-zˈənˈ Petˈɛ vorˈgədˈ-kšnˈə-sˈ-tˈ.
translation: Exactly two criminals, who, by the way, Petja caught, were running away.
comment: An ICA relative with the parenthetical meždu pročim 'by the way' is appositive; continuation (14a) is infelicitous and (14b) felicitous.

primaryText: Kolmə-cˈə prˈistupnˈik-sˈ vorˈgədˈ-kšnˈə-sˈ no Petˈɛ izˈ-əzˈə kunda sonˈ.
translation: The third criminal was also running away, but Petja did not catch him.
context: Uttered as a continuation of (13): Rovnaj kaftə prˈistupnˈik-nˈə-nˈ kona-tˈnˈə-nˈ meždu pročim kunda-zˈənˈ Petˈɛ vorˈgədˈ-kšnˈə-sˈ-tˈ. 'Exactly two criminals, who, by the way, Petja caught, were running away.'
comment: A continuation adding a third criminal who was running away is infelicitous after the ICA relative in (13), confirming its appositive reading.

primaryText: Petˈɛ kunda-zˈə kolmə-cˈə prˈistupnˈik-tˈ no son kɛš-sˈ saraj-sə.
translation: Peter also caught the third criminal, but he was hiding in a barn.
context: Uttered as a continuation of (13): Rovnaj kaftə prˈistupnˈik-nˈə-nˈ kona-tˈnˈə-nˈ meždu pročim kunda-zˈənˈ Petˈɛ vorˈgədˈ-kšnˈə-sˈ-tˈ. 'Exactly two criminals, who, by the way, Petja caught, were running away.'
comment: A continuation adding a third caught criminal who was not running away is felicitous after the ICA relative in (13), as the appositive reading allows.

primaryText: Koj kona prˈistupnˈik-nˈə-nˈ kona-tˈnˈə-nˈ kunda-zˈənˈ Petˈɛ vorˈgədˈ-kšnˈə-sˈ-tˈ.
translation: Some criminals who Petja caught were running away.
comment: An ICA relative on an indefinite head can be restrictive (continuation (16) is felicitous); the first kona is part of the indefinite koj kona 'some', the second is the relative pronoun.

primaryText: Kolmə prˈistupnˈik-nˈə-nˈ Petˈɛ izˈ-əzˈənˈ kunda i kaft-tˈnˈə maksˈ-sˈ-tˈ prˈɛ sinˈ-cˈ.
translation: Petja did not catch three criminals and two (other) criminals surrendered.
context: Uttered as a continuation of (15): Koj kona prˈistupnˈik-nˈə-nˈ kona-tˈnˈə-nˈ kunda-zˈənˈ Petˈɛ vorˈgədˈ-kšnˈə-sˈ-tˈ. 'Some criminals who Petja caught were running away.'
comment: A continuation asserting both uncaught criminals and caught criminals who did not run away is felicitous after (15), so the ICA relative is restrictive. The book glosses izˈ-əzˈənˈ NEG.PST.3PL.O.3SG.S with no hyphen; read NEG.PST-PST.3PL.O.3SG.S, as izˈ-əzˈə in (14a).

primaryText: Lˈubovaj prˈistupnˈik-tˈ kona-nˈ palˈicija kunda-zˈə jora-j vorˈgədˈ-əm-s.
translation: Any criminal who the police caught wants to escape.
comment: An ICA relative on a free-choice head, which excludes appositive and maximalizing readings, is grammatical. The book glosses prˈistupnˈik-tˈ criminal-DEF.SG-GEN with an extra hyphen; read criminal-DEF.SG.GEN, as in (14b). The book glosses kona-nˈ 'which' with no GEN; read which-GEN, as in (26), (30), (31).

primaryText: Rovnaj kaftə prˈistupnˈik-nˈə [kona-tˈnˈə-nˈ meždu pročim kunda-zˈənˈ Petˈɛ] vorˈgədˈ-kšnˈə-sˈ-tˈ.
translation: The two criminals, who, by the way, Petja caught, were running away.
comment: A regular externally-headed relative with the parenthetical meždu pročim is appositive; it differs from (13) only in the head's case. Rovnaj is glossed 'exactly' here and 'straight' in (13).

comment: A continuation adding a third criminal who was running away is infelicitous after the external relative in (18), confirming its appositive reading.

primaryText: [Kona kaftə prˈistupnˈik-nˈə-nˈ Petˈɛ kunda-zˈənˈ] sˈinˈ vorˈgədˈ-kšnˈə-sˈ-tˈ.

comment: A continuation adding a third criminal who was running away is felicitous after the correlative in (23), as the maximalizing reading allows.

primaryText: [Kona pɛrˈɛkɛ-tˈ pidˈ-əzˈə sasˈəda-zˈə] [kona minˈ srazu seva-sˈk] son ulˈ-sˈ kapsta-nˈ.

primaryText: Pɛrˈɛkɛ-tˈ kona-nˈ pidˈ-əzˈə sasˈədə-zˈə kona-nˈ minˈ srazu seva-sˈk ulˈ-sˈ kapsta-nˈ.

primaryText: Pɛrɛkɛ-sˈ [kona-nˈ pidˈ-əzˈə sasˈədə-zˈə] [kona-nˈ minˈ srazu seva-sˈk] ulˈ-sˈ kapsta-nˈ.

primaryText: [Kona lˈubovaj prˈistupnˈik-tˈ palˈicija kunda-zˈə] son jora-j vorˈgədˈ-əm-s.

primaryText: [Kona Puškin-ənˈ jalga-nzə tˈer-nˈ-əzˈ senat-ənˈ ploščadˈ-tˈi] son ašəzˈ sa-v.

comment: A correlative with a proper-name internal head is ungrammatical; a consultant reported that it entails several Pushkins.

primaryText: Puškin-ənˈ kona-nˈ jalga-nzə tˈer-nˈ-əzˈ senat-ənˈ ploščadˈ-tˈi ašəzˈ sa-v.

primaryText: [Kona pinˈə-tˈi son maks-əzˈə jar̥cambɛlˈ-tˈ] ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ mɛlˈaft-əzˈə.
translation: Every boy remembered the dog that he gave food to.
comment: A pronoun inside a correlative cannot be bound by the main-clause quantifier; only a third person fed the dog. Indices boy_i, he_j/*i.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ mɛlˈaft-əzˈə [pinˈə-tˈ kona-nˈdˈi son maks-əzˈə jar̥cambɛlˈ-tˈ].
translation: Every boy remembered the dog that he gave food to.
comment: A pronoun inside an in-situ regular externally-headed relative can be bound; indices boy_i, he_i.

primaryText: [Pinˈə-tˈ kona-nˈdˈi son maks-əzˈə jar̥cambɛlˈ-tˈ] ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ mɛlˈaft-əzˈə.
translation: Every boy remembered the dog that he gave food to.
comment: A pronoun inside a left-dislocated regular externally-headed relative can be bound; indices boy_i, he_i.

primaryText: [Esˈ mašina-ncti kona-nˈdˈi put-f lama jarmak] Vasˈɛ dagə petˈ-əzˈə.

primaryText: [Esˈ mašina-nc kona-nˈdˈi put-f lama jarmak] Vasˈɛ dagə petˈ-əzˈə.
translation: Vasja again repaired his car that a lot of money was invested in.

primaryText: [Osal pinˈə-tˈi kona-nˈdˈi ton maks-at jar̥ca-ma] i [ečkə katə-tˈ] mon soda-sajnˈə.
translation: I know the skinny dog that you give food to and the fat cat.

primaryText: [Ečkə katə-tˈ] i [osal pinˈə-tˈi kona-nˈdˈi ton maks-at jar̥ca-ma] mon soda-sajnˈə.

primaryText: [Ečkə katə-tˈ] i [osal pinˈə-tˈ kona-nˈdˈi ton maks-at jar̥ca-ma] mon soda-sajnˈə.
translation: I know the skinny dog that you give food to and the fat cat.
comment: A regular externally-headed relative coordinates with a noun phrase in the same main-clause case.

primaryText: Uča-tˈ [kona-nˈ alˈɛ-zˈə pečk-əzˈə] ašč-i kut-tˈ ingəl-ə.
translation: The sheep that my father butchered is lying in front of the house.

primaryText: Jalga-zˈə-nˈdˈi [kona-nˈdˈi tˈaš-nˈə-nˈ kizˈ-nˈ perˈf] kurək sa-j.
translation: My friend who I have been writing to all year is coming soon.

primaryText: Jalga-zˈə-nˈdˈi [kona-nˈdˈi tˈaš-nˈə-nˈ kizˈ-nˈ perˈf] mon nˈɛj-sa kurək.
translation: I will soon see my friend to whom I have been writing all year.
comment: ICA: the object head bears the internal dative instead of the external genitive.

primaryText: Uča-sˈ [kona ašč-i kut-tˈ ingəl-ə] monˈ alˈnˈɛka-zˈə lˈɛcˈ-əzˈə.
translation: My uncle shot the sheep that is lying in front of the house.
comment: ICA with a less marked internal case: the direct-object head bears the internal nominative instead of the genitive, so the case hierarchy does not govern ICA.

primaryText: Sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ [kona jora-sˈ sa-m-s abət-tə melˈə] mon abˈiščanda-nˈ maks-əm-s knˈiga.
translation: I promised to give a book to a boy who wanted to come after lunch.
comment: ICA: the recipient head bears the internal nominative instead of the external dative.

primaryText: Pinˈə-tˈ [kona-nˈ Petˈɛ rama-zˈə] mon maks-an jar̥ca-ma.
translation: I am giving food to the dog that Petja bought.
comment: ICA: the recipient head bears the internal genitive instead of the external dative.

primaryText: Pinˈə-tˈi [kona-nˈdˈi Petˈa maksˈ-i jar̥ca-ma] mon pelˈ-an.
translation: I am afraid of the dog that Petja gave food to.
comment: ICA with an oblique external case: the head, the ablative argument of pelˈəms 'fear', bears the internal dative. The book glosses Pinˈə-tˈi DEF.SG.GEN and kona-nˈdˈi which-GEN; read DEF.SG.DAT and which-DAT, as the ABL ← DAT label and the text say. The book's translation reads 'I afraid of'; read 'I am afraid of'.

primaryText: Mon pelˈ-an pinˈə-də.
translation: I am afraid of the dog.
comment: Baseline: pelˈəms 'fear' takes an ablative argument.

primaryText: Mon pelˈ-inˈə pinˈə-tˈ.
translation: I am afraid of the dog.
comment: The slash alternative of (126): pelˈəms 'fear' cannot take a genitive direct object with objective conjugation. The translation is the one printed for the whole example.

primaryText: Oš-tˈ [kona-nˈ mon kelˈk-sa] Katˈɛ erˈɛ-j.
translation: Katja lives in the city that I love.
comment: ICA with an oblique external case: the locative head of erˈɛms 'live' bears the internal genitive instead of the inessive.

primaryText: Katˈɛ erˈɛ-j oš-sə.
translation: Katja lives in the city.
comment: Baseline for (127): the noun takes the inessive in the main clause.

primaryText: Kurtkə-tˈ [kona-nˈ mon rama-jnˈə] brad-əzˈə targa-j modamar̥ˈ-tˈ.
translation: My brother is digging potatoes wearing the jacket that I bought.
comment: ICA is severely degraded or impossible when the intended inessive head is neither an argument nor a typical adjunct of the main predicate, so its role cannot be recovered without the external case.

primaryText: Brad-əzˈə targa-j modamar̥ˈ-tˈ sɛngɛrˈɛ kurtkə-sə.
translation: My brother is digging potatoes wearing a green jacket.
comment: Baseline for (129): 'wearing a jacket' takes the inessive. The book glosses Brad-əzˈə 'bother'; read 'brother', as in (129).

primaryText: Minˈ nˈɛj-əsˈk sˈɛ pinˈə-tˈ [kona-də baška aš-əlˈ ki-nˈdˈi sala-m-s sivəlˈ-tˈ].
translation: We noticed this dog, except for which no one would steal the meat.
comment: Externally headed relative: kona has an ablative form as the complement of the postposition baška 'except for'.

primaryText: Minˈ karšə vasˈft-əsˈk pinˈə-tˈ [kona-də pel̥ˈ-tˈamə].
translation: We encountered the dog that we are afraid of.
comment: Ablative kona is ungrammatical as the argument of pelˈəms 'fear'. The translation is printed as intended.

primaryText: Ručka-sˈ [kona-sə mon sˈormad-anˈ] ravžə.
translation: The pen with which I am writing is black.
comment: kona has no inessive form. The translation is printed as intended.

primaryText: Mon kelˈk-sa oš-tˈ [kona-stə minˈ tu-mə].
translation: I love the city which we moved from.
comment: kona has no elative form. The translation is printed as intended.

primaryText: Minˈ karšə vasˈft-əsˈk pinˈə-tˈ [kona-nˈ ezdə pel̥ˈ-tˈamə].
translation: We encountered the dog that we are afraid of.
comment: Minimal pair with (132): genitive kona plus the postposition ezdə 'in.ABL' replaces the missing ablative.

primaryText: Ručka-sˈ [kona-nˈ mar̥tə mon sˈormad-anˈ] ravžə.
translation: The pen with which I am writing is black.
comment: Minimal pair with (133): genitive kona plus the postposition mar̥tə 'with' replaces the missing inessive.

primaryText: Polka-sˈ [kona-nˈ lank-stə mešok-sˈ bɛcˈkafcˈ] sˈinˈdˈ-əv-sˈ.
translation: The shelf that the bag fell from broke.
comment: Genitive kona plus the postposition lank-stə 'top.EL' replaces the missing elative.

primaryText: Polka-sˈ [kona-stə mešok-sˈ bɛcˈkafcˈ] sˈinˈdˈ-əv-sˈ.
translation: The shelf that the bag fell from broke.
comment: The slash alternative of (137): elative kona-stə is ungrammatical.

primaryText: Pinˈə-də [kona-nˈ ezdə mon pelˈ-an] ašč-i ulˈcˈɛ-tˈ kučka-sə.
translation: The dog that I am afraid of is standing in the middle of the street.
comment: ICA of an oblique internal case: the head bears the ablative assigned inside the relative clause while kona is genitive under the postposition ezdə, so the head and kona differ in marking.

primaryText: Ručka-sə [kona-nˈ mar̥tə mon sˈormad-anˈ] ravžə.
translation: The pen with which I am writing is black.
comment: ICA of the inessive on the head while kona is genitive under mar̥tə 'with'.

primaryText: Polka-stə [kona-nˈ lank-stə mešok-sˈ bɛcˈkafcˈ] sˈinˈdˈ-əv-sˈ.
translation: The shelf that the bag fell from broke.
comment: ICA of the elative on the head while kona is genitive under lank-stə 'top.EL'.

primaryText: Pinˈə-tˈ [kona-nˈ ezdə mon pelˈ-an] ašč-i ulˈcˈɛ-tˈ kučka-sə.

comment: The head can instead attract the genitive that kona bears under the postposition (cf. (138)).

primaryText: Ručka-tˈ [kona-nˈ mar̥tə mon sˈormad-anˈ] ravžə.
translation: The pen with which I am writing is black.
comment: The head attracts the genitive of kona under mar̥tə (cf. (139)). The book glosses Ručka-tˈ pen-IN; read pen-DEF.SG.GEN, as the NOM ← GEN label, the definite genitive -tˈ and the text say. The book's translation reads 'with which I am writing with'; the second 'with' is dropped.

primaryText: Lauka-s [kona-nˈdˈi tu-sˈ monˈ brada-zˈə] af kunarə panžə-v-sˈ.
translation: The store where my brother went has opened recently.
comment: ICA of the illative on the head while kona, which has no illative, is dative.

primaryText: Lauka-s [kona-s tu-sˈ monˈ brada-zˈə] af kunarə panžə-v-sˈ.

primaryText: Alaša-sə [kona-nˈ esə soka-tamə paksˈɛ] erˈavˈ-i tˈišə.
translation: The horse with which we plow the field needs grass.
comment: ICA of the inessive instead of the external dative. The book prints no mark, but the text calls (144) 'somewhat degraded, but not fully unacceptable' with the head 'intended to function as an adjunct'; the head here is the dative experiencer of erˈavˈi 'need', and the description fits (145) (an inessive adjunct 'on the horse', marked ??) better. primaryText: Alaša-də [kona-nˈ ezdə mon pelˈ-an] erˈavˈ-i molˈ-əm-s oš-u.
translation: We need to go to the city on the horse that I am afraid of.
comment: ICA of the ablative is degraded when the head is an inessive adjunct of the main clause. The text does not discuss (145) separately.

primaryText: Vasˈɛ panˈž-əzˈə potmə-nc ava-ncti.
translation: Vasja told everything to his wife.
comment: The idiom panˈžəms potmə 'open up, tell everything' in a simple clause. The book glosses ava-ncti 'wife' DEF.SG.DAT here; read 3SG.POSS.SG.DAT, as in (14), (15) (the definite dative would be -tˈi).

primaryText: Sˈedˈi-cˈə af oza-j.
translation: You are worried.
comment: The idiom sˈedˈijəc af ozaj 'someone's heart does not sit' (be worried) in a simple clause.

primaryText: Potmə-nc [kona-nˈ Vasˈɛ panˈž-əzˈə ava-ncti] kunarə af maks-i pokoj.

comment: The idiom panˈžəms potmə split between an ICA head and the relative clause verb is grammatical.

primaryText: Potmə-c [kona-nˈ Vasˈɛ panˈž-əzˈə ava-ncti] kunarə af maks-i pokoj.

primaryText: Sˈedˈi-cˈə-nˈ [kona af oza-j] van-ft-k.

primaryText: Potmə-c [kona kunarə af maks-i pokoj] Vasˈɛ panˈžˈ-əzˈə ava-ncti.

primaryText: Sˈedˈij-əc [kona-nˈ Paša pɛk van-fci] af oza-j.

primaryText: Sˈedˈij-ənc [kona-nˈ Paša pɛk van-fci] af oza-j.
translation: His heart, which Pasha takes care of, is not calm.

primaryText: Vasˈɛ [esˈ prˈa-nc] arala-si lomatˈ-tˈnˈə-nˈ ezdə.

primaryText: Vanˈɛ varˈaga-nc mu-zˈə.
translation: Vanja found his mitten.
comment: Without esˈ the possessive suffix may refer to the subject or to another individual (varˈaga-nc_i/j). The book glosses mu-zˈə PST.3SG.O.SG.S; read PST.3SG.O.3SG.S, the form printed for every other objective-conjugation verb in the section. Cited from Toldova & Shalganova (2018: 654).

primaryText: Mon tu-šənd-an esˈ velˈə-zə-n.
translation: I am going to my village.
comment: The possessive suffix on a noun with esˈ agrees with the reflexive's binder (Mon_i ... esˈ_i). Cited from Toldova & Shalganova (2018: 654).

primaryText: Esˈ kud-ənc [kona-nˈ Vasˈɛ mi-zˈə] tˈɛnˈi ašč-i savə.

primaryText: Esˈ kud-əc [kona-nˈ Vasˈɛ mi-zˈə] tˈɛnˈi ašč-i savə.
translation: The house of his that Vasja sold is now empty.
comment: The reflexive in an external-case head cannot be bound inside the relative clause. The book glosses ašč-i be-PST.3[SG]; read be-NPST.3[SG], as in (42), (44) and the present-tense translation.

primaryText: ⟨...⟩ a esˈ velˈə-nˈ sˈora-nˈəkə tu-j̊-tˈ lˈijɛ velˈ-i sˈor... sˈtˈərˈ-ənˈdˈi.

primaryText: Tˈɛ knˈiga-sˈ maks-i esˈ luv-ij-ənzə-nˈdˈi nadˈəja-ma.
translation: This book gives its readers hope.

primaryText: Esˈ luv-ij-ənzə kelk-sazˈ tˈɛ knˈiga-tˈ.
translation: Its readers love this book.
comment: esˈ in subject position cannot take the non-c-commanding inanimate object as antecedent.

primaryText: Esˈ luv-ij-ənzə-nˈdˈi [kona-tˈnˈə-nˈdˈi tˈɛ knˈiga-sˈ maks-i nadˈəja-ma] uč-ij̊-tˈ pe.
translation: Its readers whom this book gave hope to are waiting for the sequel.
comment: esˈ in an ICA head is bound by an inanimate antecedent inside the relative clause (Esˈ_i ... knˈiga-sˈ_i).

primaryText: Esˈ fundamənt-ənc [kona-nˈ velˈdˈə tˈɛ kucˈ ašč-i] nˈingə af naksad-i.
translation: Its foundation, thanks to which this house is standing, is not rotting.
comment: esˈ in an ICA head is bound by an inanimate antecedent inside the relative clause (Esˈ_i ... kucˈ_i).

primaryText: Esˈ luv-ij-ənzə [kona-tˈnˈə-nˈdˈi tˈɛ knˈiga-sˈ maks-i nadˈəja-ma] uč-ij̊-tˈ pe.
translation: Its readers whom this book gave hope to are waiting for the continuation sequel.
comment: esˈ in an external-case head cannot be bound inside the relative clause. The translation reads 'the continuation sequel' as printed; (41) has 'the sequel'.

primaryText: Esˈ fundamənt-əc [kona-nˈ velˈdˈə tˈɛ kucˈ ašč-i] nˈingə af naksad-i.
translation: Its foundation, thanks to which this house is standing, is not rotting.
comment: esˈ in an external-case head cannot be bound inside the relative clause.

primaryText: Esˈ mašina-ncti [kona-nˈdˈi put-f lama jarmak] Vasˈɛ dagə petˈ-əzˈə.
translation: Vasja again repaired his car into which a lot of money had been invested.
comment: esˈ in an ICA head is bound by the matrix subject (Esˈ_i ... Vasˈɛ_i). Repeated from (3:67), where the whole relative is bracketed and the translation differs.

primaryText: Esˈ mašina-nc [kona-nˈdˈi put-f lama jarmak] Vasˈɛ dagə petˈ-əzˈə.
translation: Vasja again repaired his car into which a lot of money has been invested.
comment: esˈ in an external-case head is bound by the matrix subject. Repeated from (3:68), which glosses kona-nˈdˈi which-GEN; the DAT gloss here matches the form, so the misprint is in (3:68).

primaryText: Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ and-əzˈə esˈ pinˈə-nc.
translation: Every boy fed his dog.
comment: A reflexive is bound by a c-commanding quantified subject (sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ_i ... esˈ_i).

primaryText: Esˈ pinˈə-c susk-əzˈə ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ.
translation: His dog bit every boy.
comment: A reflexive cannot co-vary with a quantified object that does not c-command it.

primaryText: Esˈ pinˈə-nc [kona-nˈ ɛrˈ azər-sˈ tˈerˈdˈ-si] van-ft-əzˈənˈ žuvata-tˈnˈə-nˈ.
translation: His dog that every owner calls was guarding the animals.
comment: A reflexive in an ICA head is bound by a quantifier inside the relative clause (Esˈ_i ... azər-sˈ_i).

primaryText: Esˈ pinˈə-c [kona-nˈ ɛrˈ azər-sˈ tˈerˈdˈ-si] van-ft-əzˈənˈ žuvata-tˈnˈə-nˈ.
translation: His dog that every owner calls was guarding the animals.
comment: A reflexive in an external-case head cannot be bound by a quantifier inside the relative clause.

primaryText: [Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ sˈestra-c] sˈɛv-əzˈə sonˈ kruška-nc.
translation: Every boy's sister took his cup.
comment: A personal pronoun co-varies with a quantified possessor that does not c-command it (sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ_j ... sonˈ_i/j).

primaryText: Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ soda-si [što sonˈ dˈɛdˈa-c kurək sa-j].
translation: Every boy knows that his mother will come soon.
comment: A personal pronoun in an embedded clause is bound by a c-commanding non-local quantifier (sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ_j ... sonˈ_i/j). Repeated from (3:61).

primaryText: Sonˈ knˈiga-c ašč-i ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ komnata-sə-nzə.
translation: His book is in every boy's room.
comment: A pronoun cannot be bound by a quantifier it c-commands (Sonˈ_i/*j ... sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ_j). Repeated from (3:62). The book glosses komnata 'book'; read 'room', as in the translation and in (3:62).

primaryText: Sonˈ kelˈgəma igruška-nc [kona-nˈ [ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ dˈɛdˈa-c] kand-əzˈə balˈnˈica-s] lˈezd-i af pelˈə-m-s vrač-də.
translation: His favorite toy that every boy's mother brought to the hospital helps him not to be afraid of doctors.
comment: A pronoun in an ICA head co-varies with a quantified possessor inside the relative-clause subject (Sonˈ_i/j ... sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ_j). The book marks the gap with an underscore before balˈnˈica-s; omitted here.

primaryText: Sonˈ kelˈgəma igruška-c [kona-nˈ [ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ dˈɛdˈa-c] kand-əzˈə balˈnˈica-s] lˈezd-i af pelˈə-m-s vrač-də.
translation: His favorite toy that every boy's mother brought to the hospital helps him not to be afraid of doctors.
comment: A pronoun in an external-case head also co-varies with the quantifier inside the relative clause. The book marks the gap with an underscore before balˈnˈica-s; omitted here.

primaryText: Sonˈ kelˈgəma igruška-c [kona ašč-i ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ komnata-sə] vrač-t urˈada-zˈ.
translation: Doctors took away his favorite toy that is in every boy's room.
comment: Binding into an ICA head succeeds even though the gap (subject) is higher than the quantifier. The book marks the gap with an underscore after kona; omitted here.

primaryText: Sonˈ kelˈgəma igruška-nc [kona ašč-i ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ komnata-sə] vrač-t urˈada-zˈ.
translation: Doctors took away his favorite toy that is in every boy's room.
comment: Binding into an external-case head succeeds with the gap higher than the quantifier. The book marks the gap with an underscore after kona; omitted here.

primaryText: Sonˈ knˈiga-c ašč-i ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ komnata-sə-nzə.
translation: His book is in every boy's room.
comment: Repeats (61): a pronoun cannot be bound by a quantifier it c-commands. The book glosses komnata 'book'; read 'room', as in the translation and in (3:62).

primaryText: [Pinˈə-tˈi kona-nˈdˈi son maks-əzˈə jar̥cambɛlˈ-tˈ] ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ mɛlˈaft-əzˈə.
translation: Every boy remembered the dog that he gave food to.
comment: A matrix quantifier binds a pronoun inside a left-dislocated ICA relative (son_i ... sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ_i). Repeated from (3:63).

primaryText: [Pinˈə-tˈ kona-nˈdˈi son maks-əzˈə jar̥cambɛlˈ-tˈ] ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ mɛlˈaft-əzˈə.
translation: Every boy remembered the dog that he gave food to.
comment: A matrix quantifier binds a pronoun inside a left-dislocated external-case relative. Repeated from (3:66).

primaryText: [Kona pinˈə-tˈi son maks-əzˈə jar̥cambɛlˈ-tˈ] ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ mɛlˈaft-əzˈə.
translation: Every boy remembered the dog that he gave food to.
comment: A matrix quantifier cannot bind a pronoun inside a correlative clause (son_j/*i ... sˈora-nˈɛ-sˈ_i). Repeated from (3:64).

primaryText: Ɛrˈ tˈɛdˈɛ-tˈi [kona kelˈk-si esˈ idˈ-ənc] škola-nˈkə lˈezd-i.
translation: Our school helps every mother who loves her child.
comment: A reflexive in the relative clause is bound by the quantified external-case head; the gap c-commands the reflexive. The book glosses tˈɛdˈɛ-tˈi DEF.SG.GEN; the form is the definite dative (genitive -tˈ, cf. (75)) and 'help' governs the dative, as the DAT ← NOM label of (74) shows. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ tˈɛdˈɛ-sˈ [kona-nˈ esˈ sˈora-c kelˈk-si] tˈɛ-zˈ-i pičədˈ-ə.
translation: Every mother whom her son loves is not worried.
comment: A reflexive inside the relative-clause subject is bound by the quantified external-case head although it c-commands the gap: no crossover effect. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ tˈɛdˈɛ-sˈ [kona kelˈk-si esˈ idˈ-ənc] škola-nˈkə lˈezd-i.
translation: Our school helps every mother who loves her child.
comment: A reflexive in the relative clause is bound by the quantified ICA head; the gap c-commands the reflexive. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ tˈɛdˈɛ-tˈ [kona-nˈ esˈ sˈora-c kelˈk-si] tˈɛ-zˈ-i pičədˈ-ə.
translation: Every mother whom her son loves is not worried.
comment: A reflexive inside the relative-clause subject is bound by the quantified ICA head although it c-commands the gap: no crossover effect. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: [Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ sˈestra-c] sɛv-əzˈə sonˈ kruška-nc.
translation: Every boy's sister took his cup.
comment: A quantified possessor binds a personal pronoun, not the reflexive, which the book prints as the starred variant ( / *esˈ).

primaryText: Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ sˈestra-nc [kona sɛv-əzˈə sonˈ igruška-nc] učitˈəlˈ-sˈ krˈikənda-zˈə.
translation: The teacher scolded every boy's sister who took his toy.
comment: A pronoun in the relative clause is bound by the quantified possessor of an external-case head; the gap c-commands the pronoun. The book glosses sɛv-əzˈə PST.3SG.O3SG.S; read PST.3SG.O.3SG.S. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ sˈestra-c [kona-nˈ sonˈ učitˈəlˈ-c šna-zˈə] lˈez-sˈ kud-ənˈ zadanˈija-tˈ.
translation: Every boy's sister whom his teacher praised helped with the homework.
comment: A pronoun inside the relative-clause subject is bound by the quantified possessor of an external-case head: no secondary crossover effect. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ sˈestra-c [kona sɛv-əzˈə sonˈ igruška-nc] učitˈəlˈ-sˈ krˈikənda-zˈə.
translation: The teacher scolded every boy's sister who took his toy.
comment: A pronoun in the relative clause is bound by the quantified possessor of an ICA head; the gap c-commands the pronoun. The book glosses sɛv-əzˈə PST.3SG.O3SG.S; read PST.3SG.O.3SG.S. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ sˈestra-nc [kona-nˈ sonˈ učitˈəlˈ-c šna-zˈə] lˈez-sˈ kud-ənˈ zadanˈija-tˈ.
translation: Every boy's sister whom his teacher praised helped with the homework.
comment: A pronoun inside the relative-clause subject is bound by the quantified possessor of an ICA head: no secondary crossover effect. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ pisatˈəlˈ-tˈ azks-əc [kona-nˈ sonˈ jalga-c af kelˈk-si] adˈəla-j kalˈdˈəv-stə.
translation: Every writer's story that his friend does not like ends badly.
comment: With an agent-like quantified dependent of an external-case head, a pronoun c-commanding the gap is still bound: no crossover effect. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ɛrˈ pisatˈəlˈ-tˈ azks-ənc [kona-nˈ sonˈ jalga-c af kelˈk-si] adˈəla-j kalˈdˈəv-stə.
translation: Every writer's story that his friend does not like ends badly.
comment: With an agent-like quantified dependent of an ICA head, a pronoun c-commanding the gap is still bound: no crossover effect. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Ava-sˈ rama-zˈə kut-tˈ.
comment: Free argument order in Moksha: the SVO order. The book prints no translation.

primaryText: Ava-sˈ kut-tˈ rama-zˈə.
comment: Free argument order in Moksha: the SOV order. The book prints no translation.

comment: Free argument order in Moksha: the OSV order. The book prints no translation.

primaryText: Kut-tˈ rama-zˈə ava-sˈ.
comment: Free argument order in Moksha: the OVS order. The book prints no translation.

primaryText: [Kodamə sˈora-nˈə-tˈ] esˈ pinˈə-c susk-əzˈə?
translation: Which boy did his dog bite?
comment: A wh-moved quantifier crosses a reflexive it binds with no crossover effect (sˈora-nˈə-tˈ_i ... esˈ_i). The book glosses susk-əzˈə bit-PST.3SG.O.3.SG.S; read bite-PST.3SG.O.3SG.S as in (56). The diminutive is printed -nˈə- here, -nˈɛ- elsewhere. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: [Ɛrˈ pisatˈəlˈ-tˈ kodamə azks-ənc] sonˈ jalga-c af kelˈk-si?
translation: Which story by every writer his friend does not like?
comment: A wh-phrase containing a quantifier crosses a pronoun the quantifier binds with no crossover effect (pisatˈəlˈ-tˈ_i ... sonˈ_i). The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Katˈɛ mɛrˈg-sˈ što son nˈɛj-əzˈə Anna-nˈ fətəgrafija-nc.
translation: Katja said that she saw Anna's photo.
comment: A pronoun cannot corefer with a name it c-commands (son_j/*i ... Anna-nˈ_i).

primaryText: Son sˈormad-əzˈə Puškin-ənˈ azks-ənc.
translation: He wrote Pushkin's story.
comment: A pronoun cannot corefer with a name it c-commands (Son_j/*i ... Puškin-ənˈ_i).

primaryText: Katˈɛ az-ənd-əzˈə [kodamə Anna-nˈ fətəgrafija-nc] son nˈɛj-əzˈə.
translation: Katja said which photo of Anna she saw.
comment: Clause-internal wh-movement does not obviate Condition C (Anna-nˈ_j ... son_i/*j). The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: [Kodamə Puškin-ənˈ azks-ənc] son sˈormad-əzˈə?
translation: Which story of Pushkin did he write?
comment: Clause-internal wh-movement does not obviate Condition C (Puškin-ənˈ_j ... son_i/*j). The book prints Pušnik-ənˈ; read Puškin-ənˈ, as the gloss 'Pushkin' and (98) show. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: [Kodamə Puškin-ənˈ knˈiga-nc] ton soda-sak što son sˈormad-əzˈə dača-sə?
translation: Which book of Pushkin you know that he wrote at the country house?
comment: Long-distance wh-movement obviates Condition C for some speakers: the coreferent index is marked % (son_i/%j ... Puškin-ənˈ_j). The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Katˈɛ az-ənd-əzˈə [kodamə Anna-nˈ fətəgrafija-nc] Miša arˈsˈ-i što son nˈɛj-əzˈə?
translation: Katja said which photo of Anna Misha thinks she saw.
comment: Long-distance wh-movement does not obviate Condition C here (Anna-nˈ_j ... son_i/*j); the book prints the translation as 'Intended'. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Puškin-ənˈ knˈiga-c [kona-nˈ son tˈɛštˈ-əzˈə Pavləfskɛj dača-sə] ašč-i biblˈiatˈeka-sə-nək.
translation: Pushkin's book that he wrote in the country house in Pavlovsk is in our library.
comment: A name in an external-case head can corefer with a pronoun in the relative clause (Puškin-ənˈ_j ... son_i/j). The book glosses Pavləfskɛj as Pavlosk’s; read Pavlovsk’s, as in the translation. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Puškin-ənˈ knˈiga-nc [kona-nˈ son tˈɛštˈ-əzˈə Pavləfskɛj dača-sə] ašč-i biblˈiatˈeka-sə-nək.
translation: Pushkin's book that he wrote in the country house in Pavlovsk is in our library.
comment: A name in an ICA head cannot corefer with a pronoun in the relative clause (Puškin-ənˈ_j ... son_i/*j). The book glosses Pavləfskɛj as Pavlosk’s; read Pavlovsk’s, as in the translation. The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Anna-nˈ jalga-nc [kona-nˈdˈi son kunarə af zvonˈ-cˈ-i] mon vasˈft-inˈə.
translation: I met Anna's friend who she had not called for a while.
comment: In a neutral context a name in an external-case head can corefer with a pronoun in the relative clause (Anna-nˈ_j ... son_i/j). The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Anna-nˈ jalga-ncti [kona-nˈdˈi son kunarə af zvonˈ-cˈ-i] mon vasˈft-inˈə.
translation: I met Anna's friend who she had not called for a while.
comment: In a neutral context a name in an ICA head cannot corefer with a pronoun in the relative clause (Anna-nˈ_j ... son_i/*j). The book marks the gap with an underscore; omitted here.

primaryText: Minˈ jorda-sˈk [škaf-tˈi [kona-nˈdˈi mon put-inˈə fətəgrafijə-tˈnˈə-nˈ] ].
translation: We threw away the cupboard where I put the photos.
comment: A relative with ICA cannot follow the main-clause predicate (postverbal object position, sentence-final). Repeats ch. 3 (33), which glosses škaf 'cabinet', brackets the relative flat and translates 'where I had put'.

primaryText: [Škaf-tˈi [kona-nˈdˈi mon put-inˈə fətəgrafijə-tˈnˈə-nˈ] ] minˈ jorda-sˈk.
translation: We threw away the cupboard where I put the photos.
comment: The same object relative with ICA at the left edge is grammatical. Repeats ch. 3 (32), which glosses škaf 'cabinet' and translates 'where I had put'.

primaryText: Sa-j kizə-tˈ [sˈora-nˈɛ-tˈ [kona-nˈ Katˈɛ tona-ft-əzˈə luv-əmə] ] škola-v molˈ-i.
translation: Next year the boy whom Katja teaches to read will go to school.
comment: A relative with ICA can follow a left-peripheral adjunct (sa-j kizə-tˈ 'next year'), which the book takes to be base-generated there. Repeats ch. 3 (39), translated there 'the boy Katja taught to read will start school'.

primaryText: Katˈɛ [škaf-tˈi [kona-nˈdˈi mon put-inˈə fətəgrafijə-tˈnˈə-nˈ] ] jorda-zˈə.
translation: Katja threw away the cupboard where I put the photos.
comment: A relative with ICA after a main-clause argument is accepted only by some speakers (defective intervention for the others). Repeats ch. 3 (42). The book's translation reads 'cubboard'; read 'cupboard'.

primaryText: Uča-tˈnˈə [kona-tˈnˈə ašč-iˈj̊-t kut-tˈ ingəl-ə] monˈ alˈnˈɛka-zˈə lˈɛcˈ-əzˈənˈ.
translation: My uncle shot the sheep that are in front of the house.
comment: A direct-object relative with ICA is also displaced to the left, and the main verb agrees with it in number (3PL object), against a labeling account of the displacement.

primaryText: [Pinˈə-tˈnˈ-nˈdˈi [kona-tˈnˈ-nˈdˈi maks-inˈə jar̥ca-ma-tˈ] ] ašč-ij̊-tˈ dvor-sə.
translation: The dogs that I gave food to are in the yard.
comment: A subject DP with ICA lacks main-clause case but triggers plural subject agreement on the main verb.

primaryText: [Jalga-zˈə-nˈdˈi [kona-nˈdˈi mon zvonˈ-ənˈ] ] navernə sɛv-inˈə knˈiga-tˈ.
translation: Probably my friend whom I called to has taken the book.
comment: A subject relative with ICA precedes the TP-level adverb navernə 'probably', so subjects are displaced too. The main verb sɛv-inˈə is glossed take-PST.3.O.1SG.S, a 1SG subject form, although the translation makes 'my friend' the subject; kept as printed.

primaryText: [Jalga-zˈə-nˈdˈi [kona-nˈdˈi mon zvonˈ-ənˈ] ] knˈiga-tˈ navernə sɛv-inˈə.
translation: Probably my friend whom I called to has taken the book.
comment: The subject relative with ICA precedes both an object scrambled across the adverb and the adverb. The main verb sɛv-inˈə is glossed take-PST.3.O.1SG.S, a 1SG subject form, although the translation makes 'my friend' the subject; kept as printed.

primaryText: Knˈiga-tˈ navernə [jalga-zˈə-nˈdˈi [kona-nˈdˈi mon zvonˈ-ənˈ] ] sɛv-inˈə.
translation: Probably my friend whom I called to has taken the book.
comment: The subject relative with ICA cannot follow the TP-level adverb, as it could if it stayed in Spec,TP or Spec,vP. The main verb sɛv-inˈə is glossed take-PST.3.O.1SG.S, a 1SG subject form, although the translation makes 'my friend' the subject; kept as printed.

primaryText: Pinˈə-də [kona-nˈ ezdə mon pelˈ-an] ašč-i ulˈcˈɛ-tˈ kučka-sə.
translation: The dog that I am afraid of is standing in the middle of the street.
comment: Case mismatch: the head bears the ablative while kona is genitive under ezdə 'in.ABL'. Repeats ch. 3 (138).

primaryText: Pinˈə-də [kona-də mon pelˈ-an] ašč-i ulˈcˈɛ-tˈ kučka-sə.
translation: The dog that I am afraid of is standing in the middle of the street.
comment: The slash alternative of (85), which replaces kona-nˈ ezdə: ablative kona-də is ungrammatical here.

primaryText: Pinˈə-tˈ [kona-nˈ ezdə mon pelˈ-an] ašč-i ulˈcˈɛ-tˈ kučka-sə.
translation: The dog that I am afraid of is standing in the middle of the street.
comment: The head can also bear the genitive kona gets from the postposition, against a purely morphological account of the postposition. Repeats ch. 3 (141).

primaryText: Pinˈə-tˈ ezdə [kona-nˈ ezdə mon pelˈ-an] ašč-i ulˈcˈɛ-tˈ kučka-sə.
translation: The dog that I am afraid of is standing in the middle of the street.
comment: The postposition cannot be 'attracted' onto the head along with the genitive.

primaryText: Mon pelˈ-an pinˈə-tˈ ezdə.
translation: I fear the dog.
comment: Baseline for (87): genitive plus ezdə is available to a regular noun phrase as the complement of pelˈəms 'fear'.

primaryText: Lauka-s [kona-nˈdˈi tu-sˈ monˈ brada-zˈə] af kunarə panžə-v-sˈ.
translation: A store where my brother was going has opened recently.
comment: Case mismatch without a postposition: kona is dative while the head is illative. Repeats ch. 3 (143), translated there 'The store where my brother went has opened recently'.

primaryText: Lauka-s [kona-s tu-sˈ monˈ brada-zˈə] af kunarə panžə-v-sˈ.
translation: A store where my brother was going has opened recently.
comment: The slash alternative of (91): illative kona-s does not exist. Repeats the alternative of ch. 3 (143).

primaryText: Pinˈə-tˈi [kona-nˈ Petˈɛ rama-zˈə] son maksi jar̥ca-ma-tˈ.
translation: To the dog that Petja bought he is giving food.
comment: Condition C obviation: Petˈɛ inside a fronted externally headed relative can corefer with the matrix subject son 'he' (printed Petˈɛᵢ ... sonᵢ).

primaryText: Pinˈə-tˈ [kona-nˈ Petˈɛ rama-zˈə] son maksi jar̥ca-ma-tˈ.
translation: To the dog that Petja bought he is giving food.
comment: Condition C obviation also holds for a relative with ICA: Petˈɛ can corefer with the matrix subject son 'he' (printed Petˈɛᵢ ... sonᵢ), so the NP with the relative is late-merged.
